status.en: 4 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 33% fewer than the week before, most of them in Juba, Abiemnom and Mundri.
status.nb: 4 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 33 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Juba, Abiemnom og Mundri.

summary.en: President Salva Kiir lifted the state of emergency in four states ahead of the 2027 elections while ethnic violence persisted, including gunmen opening fire on a Juba-Mundri vehicle that injured two passengers and fighting in Wau town. An aid worker was killed, a Christian woman was slain for refusing a forced marriage, and 26 people were killed in an attack on SSPDF barracks in Warrap state. Jonglei authorities handed over six more abductees to Pibor and a strike by truck drivers on the main highway was resolved after a deal with the government. The UN warned that hunger is worsening sharply because of conflict and El Niño, and there were 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: President Salva Kiir opphevet unntakstilstanden i fire delstater før valget i 2027 mens etnisk vold fortsatte, inkludert skyting fra væpnede menn på et kjøretøy mellom Juba og Mundri som såret to passasjerer, og kamper i byen Wau. En hjelpearbeider ble drept, en kristen kvinne ble drept for å ha nektet et tvangs ekteskap, og 26 personer ble drept i et angrep på SSPDF-barrikader i delstaten Warrap. Myndighetene i Jonglei overleverte seks flere bortførte til Pibor, og en streik blant lastebilsjåfører på hovedveien ble løst etter en avtale med regjeringen. FN advarte om at sulten forverres kraftig på grunn av konflikt og El Niño, og det var 2 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
